L94: 
L95: We invite submissions to the 15th International Conference on Learning Representations, and welcome paper submissions from all areas of machine learning.
L96: 
L97: For any information needed that is not listed below, please submit questions using this link: cite28†Contact ICLR Program Chairs .
L98: 
L99: Questions can be directed to: program-chairs@iclr.cc.
L100: Please see the cite21†author guidelines for all submission instructions and policies. Please read these instructions carefully, as we have new policies this year regarding co-authorship, reciprocal reviewing, and the use of AI.
L101: ## Key dates
L102: 
L103: The planned dates are as follows (all times are UTC-12h, aka “Anywhere on Earth”):
L104: 
L105: Abstract deadline Sep 18, 2026 AOE
L106: 
L107: Paper deadline Sep 25, 2026 AOE
L108: 
L109: Reviews released Nov 05, 2026
L110: 
L111: Author-reviewer discussion Nov 05, 2026–Nov 18, 2026
L112: 
L113: Reviewer-AC discussion Nov 19, 2026–Dec 16, 2026
L114: 
L115: Final decisions: Dec 16, 2026
L116: ## Subject Areas
L117: 
L118: We consider a broad range of subject areas including feature learning, metric learning, compositional modeling, structured prediction, reinforcement learning, uncertainty quantification and issues regarding large-scale learning and non-convex optimization, as well as applications in vision, audio, speech, language, music, robotics, games, healthcare, biology, sustainability, economics, ethical considerations in ML, and others.
L119: 
L120: A non-exhaustive list of relevant topics:
L121:   * unsupervised, self-supervised, semi-supervised, and supervised representation learning
L122:   * transfer learning, meta learning, and lifelong learning
L123:   * reinforcement learning
L124:   * representation learning for computer vision, audio, language, and other modalities
L125:   * metric learning, kernel learning, and sparse coding
L126:   * probabilistic methods (Bayesian methods, variational inference, sampling, UQ, etc.)
L127:   * generative models
L128:   * causal reasoning
L129:   * optimization
L130:   * learning theory
L131:   * learning on graphs and other geometries & topologies
L132:   * societal considerations including fairness, safety, privacy
L133:   * visualization or interpretation of learned representations
L134:   * datasets and benchmarks
L135:   * infrastructure, software libraries, hardware, etc.
L136:   * neurosymbolic & hybrid AI systems (physics-informed, logic & formal reasoning, etc.)
L137:   * applications to robotics, autonomy, planning
L138:   * applications to neuroscience & cognitive science
L139:   * applications to physical sciences (physics, chemistry, biology, etc.)
L140:   * general machine learning (i.e., none of the above)
L141: Submissions will be double blind: reviewers cannot see author names when conducting reviews, and authors cannot see reviewer names.  Having papers on arxiv is allowed per the dual submission policy outlined in the author guidelines.
L142: ## Note for first-time submitters
L143: We are excited that improved AI tools are expanding the community of researchers, and we encourage submissions from authors new to ICLR! However, we also feel that it is important to emphasize that the ICLR peer review process involves an enormous amount of volunteer work by thousands of people, and we ask that you respect their time. A typical ICLR paper involves significantly more work than goes into a course project, or than can be produced autonomously by any current AI agent.
L144: Because of the open nature of ICLR’s review process, all submissions (even rejected and withdrawn submissions) will remain public with authors’ names attached to them. If you are not sure your submission represents an appropriate amount of work for ICLR—or if you’re not completely certain that everything in your paper is correct—please keep working rather than submitting now. We’ll still be here next year and look forward to receiving your work then!
L145: Please also be sure to read the cite21†author guidelines carefully (particularly the quota section).
L146: ##
L147: ## Note for veteran submitters
L148: Like many of you, the ICLR leadership has been amazed to see the growth in the volume of high-quality ML research in recent years—facilitated not just by coding assistants, but also major advances in theory and research infrastructure, and increasingly close collaboration and integration with scientific and humanistic fields outside the historical domain of “core ML”.
L149: We encourage you to take this opportunity to be ambitious! Rather than submitting the same kind of project you might have submitted five years ago (and which you can now, perhaps, complete in half the time), what we want most is your slow science, and your most complete and most exciting work.

L90: AISTATS 2027 therefore adopts submission quotas modeled on the ICLR 2027 policy:
L91:   * No author may appear as a co-author on more than 12 submissions.
L92:   * Authors who do not have at least one accepted paper at ICLR, ICML, NeurIPS, or AISTATS may appear as a co-author on at most 3 submissions. Eligibility is determined by papers accepted for publication by the abstract submission deadline, as recorded in the author's OpenReview profile.
L93:   * Exemption of reciprocal reviewing on the basis of "all authors are unqualified" can only be requested for one paper per author. As a consequence, someone not qualified for reviewing can submit at most one single-author paper. Such an author may still appear on other submissions, provided that another co-author is nominated to review or qualifies for a different exemption.
L94: Submissions in excess of either quota will be flagged during the abstract submission period. If they are still exceeded at the time of full paper submission, we will randomly desk-reject excess submissions until every author is under quota.
L95: 
L96: Update September 24, 2026: update on the quota of exemption of reciprocal reviewing.
L97: ## Changes of Title/Abstract/Authorship
L98: The author list submitted at the abstract submission deadline is final. No author may be added or removed after the abstract submission deadline, under any circumstances, including after acceptance and during the camera-ready phase. This is to avoid new unforeseen conflicts of interest after the bidding, which will start immediately after the abstract submission deadline, and to enforce the reciprocal reviewing and quota policies.
L99: Please make sure that all authors are listed, with correct OpenReview profiles, at the time of abstract submission. The author order can be changed after the paper is accepted.
L100: Submissions violating these rules will be deleted after the paper submission deadline without review. Major changes to the title and abstract after the abstract deadline will also be flagged for desk rejection.
L101: ## Formatting and Supplementary Material
L102: Submissions are limited to 8 pages (excluding references, the AI Use Statement, the reproducibility checklist, and additional appendices) using the LaTeX style file we will provide on this webpage on this webpage (the page limit will be 9 for camera-ready submissions). The number of pages containing only citations, the AI Use Statement, the reproducibility checklist, and appendices (such as proof details) is not limited. Papers with main text beyond the page limit will be desk-rejected.
L103: Supplementary material. Any additional supplementary material must be submitted by the full paper submission deadline, either as part of the main submission PDF (after the references, the AI Use Statement, and the reproducibility checklist) or separately in a single PDF file or a ZIP file for other formats/more files (such as code or videos).
L104: It is the authors' responsibility that any supplementary material does not conflict in content with the main paper (e.g., the separately uploaded additional material is not an updated version of the one appended to the manuscript). There is no separate supplementary material deadline.
L105: Formatting information (including LaTeX style files): cite22†https://aistats.org/aistats2027/AISTATS2027PaperPack.zip†aistats.org L106: ## Reciprocal Reviewing (Reviewer Nomination)
L107: 
L108: AISTATS relies on its authors to serve as reviewers: each submission triggers at least three full reviews, and the growth in submissions makes it impossible to maintain review quality without the participation of the authors. Following the ICML 2026 and NeurIPS 2026 policies, the following rules apply to all submissions.
L109: Per-submission requirement. For each submission, the authors must nominate, in the submission form, one of the authors as a reciprocal reviewer for AISTATS 2027. Nominated reviewers must have sufficient expertise in the relevant field: research experience at least equivalent to a second-year PhD student in machine learning, statistics, or a related field, and multiple publications at the top AI/ML conferences, or multiple top journal papers in statistics or related fields.
L110: Exemption. If no author of a submission cannot be nominated, exemptions will be granted on exceptionnal basis. The exemption must be requested and justified through this form cite23†https://forms.gle/Wi25nF3227UMzvnF6†forms.gle ; unjustified exemption requests will be treated as a missing nomination. Exemption of reciprocal reviewing on the basis of "all authors are unqualified" can only be requested for one paper per author.
L111: As a consequence, someone not qualified for reviewing can submit at most one single-author paper. Such an author may still appear on other submissions, provided that another co-author is nominated to review or qualifies for a different exemption.
L112: Consequences. Submissions that do not satisfy the per-submission requirement may be desk-rejected. Nominated reviewers who fail to deliver complete, timely, high-quality reviews, or who do not take part in the discussion phase, may have the submission on which they were nominated — and their other submissions — desk-rejected. In addition, authors who are also reviewers will not see the reviews of their own submission(s) until they have completed all of their assigned reviews.
L113: Reviews that are evidently produced by an LLM in violation of the reviewer policy count as missing reviews.
L114: Incentives. Reviewers who deliver high-quality, timely reviews will be recognized: the top reviewers, as identified by area chairs, will be publicly acknowledged and receive Top Reviewer awards. All reviewers will have access, during the discussion phase, to the AI factual-correctness review of the papers they review (see below).
L115: 
L116: Update September 23, 2026: adding the reciprocal reviewing exemption form.
L117: Update September 24, 2026: clarification added regarding the exemption in cases involving non-qualified authors.
L118: ## AI Review of Submissions
L119: 
L120: New in 2027: all submissions will go through an AI review, generated by an LLM-based system operated by the conference. The purpose of this review is to help detect factual errors and support the human reviewing process, not to replace it:
L121:   * Scope. The AI review targets factual correctness: incorrect or unsupported claims, errors or gaps in proofs, inconsistencies between the text, tables, and figures, mismatches between the described and reported experimental setup, and misattributed related work. It does not assess significance or novelty, it does not produce a score, and it makes no recommendation.
L122:   * Not visible to reviewers while reviewing. Human reviewers will not have access to the AI review while writing their own reviews, so that their independent judgement is preserved.
L123:   * Visible to authors at rebuttal time. The AI review will be released to the authors together with the human reviews at the start of the rebuttal period (November 16, 2026), so that authors can respond to it.
L124:   * Visible to reviewers and area chairs at discussion time. The AI review, and the authors' response to it, will be made available to reviewers and area chairs during the discussion phase.
L125:   * Decisions remain human. The AI review is one input among others; all decisions are made by the area chairs, senior area chairs, and program chairs based on the human reviews and discussion.
L126:   * Confidentiality. Submissions will be processed by a privacy-compliant system under the same confidentiality requirements as the human review process; submissions will not be used to train models.
L127: Further details on the AI review, including the exact format and how authors and reviewers are expected to engage with it, will be posted on the conference website before the submission deadline.
L128: Human reviewers remain bound by the reviewer policy on LLMs: reviewers must not delegate their judgement and critique of a submission to an LLM, must not produce their reviews with an LLM, and must not enter submission content into non-privacy-compliant tools. Violations may lead to sanctions, including the desk rejection of the reviewer's own submissions.
L129: ## Anonymization Requirements
L130: The AISTATS review process is double-blind. All submissions must be anonymized and may not contain any information that can violate the double-blind reviewing policy, such as the author names or their affiliations, acknowledgements, or links that can infer any author's identity or institution. Self-citations are allowed as long as anonymity is preserved. It is up to the author's discretion how best to preserve anonymity when including self-citations.
L131: Possibilities include: leaving out a self-citation, including it but replacing the citation text with "removed for anonymous submission," or leaving the citation as-is (being referred to in third person, like other citations).
L132: We suggest the authors refrain from advertising the preprint on social media or in the press while under submission to AISTATS. Preprints must not be explicitly identified as an AISTATS submission at any time during the review period (i.e., from the abstract submission deadline until the communication of the accept/reject decision). If it is being posted to arXiv (or similar sites), we suggest using a neutral (non-AISTATS) format.
L133: Authors are also allowed to give talks on the work(s) submitted to AISTATS during the review, but these talks should not identify papers as AISTATS submissions.
L134: ## Dual Submissions
L135: Submitted manuscripts should not have been previously published in a journal or in the proceedings of a conference, and should not be under consideration for publication at another conference at any point during the AISTATS review process. Submissions as extended abstracts (4 pages or less) to workshops or non-archival venues (without a proceedings) will not be considered a concurrent submission.
L136: Tech reports (on arXiv or similar sites) and short papers in workshops without archival proceedings do not count as prior publication.
L137: ## Confidentiality
L138: 
L139: The reviewers and area chairs of your paper will have access to your paper (and supplementary material). In addition, the program chairs and workflow chairs will have access to all papers. Everyone having access to papers is instructed to keep them confidential during the review process and delete them after the final decisions. Submissions are also processed by the conference's AI review system (see cite17†AI Review of Submissions ), under the same confidentiality requirements.
L140: Reviews will be visible to area chairs, program chairs, and workflow chairs throughout the process. Reviewers will get access to other reviews for a paper during the rebuttal phase, and to the AI review during the discussion phase.
L141: 
L142: Author names will be visible to program chairs and workflow chairs. Reviewers and area chairs will not know the author names at any stage of the process. Reviewer names are visible to the area chairs, workflow chairs, and program chairs.
L143: ## Use of Generative AI by Authors
L144: 
L145: (aligned with ICLR policy -- cite24†https://iclr.cc/Conferences/2027/AIPolicyForAuthors†iclr.cc )
L146: ### Policy on LLM use for research and writing papers
L147: 
L148: We recognize that research is now often carried out in hybrid human–AI workflows: LLMs and other generative AI tools are used at all stages, varying in sophistication from formulating proofs to formatting tables. Consequently, the use of generative AI tools to assist in research or writing is allowed at AISTATS 2027, under the following conditions.
L149: Authors are fully responsible for the content of their submission. This includes any content generated by AI tools. A substantial falsehood, instance of plagiarism, fabricated or misattributed reference, or misrepresentation produced by an LLM is considered scientific misconduct on the part of the paper's authors, and may lead to desk rejection of the paper and to the authors being reported to the AISTATS board. LLMs are not eligible for authorship.
L150: Clarity of writing is a requirement. Reviewers and area chairs are instructed to assess clarity as a first-class criterion. Submissions whose writing is unclear, verbose, repetitive, unfocused, or padded with generic content — as is typical of insufficiently edited AI-generated papers — are candidates for rejection, and may be desk-rejected by the area chairs before review.
L151: Submitting low-quality AI-generated content is an abuse of the peer-review process; it may result in the desk rejection of the violating submission or of all submissions by the same authors.
L152: ### Mandatory AI Use Statement
L153: We ask that authors explicitly state how they used LLMs and other generative AI tools in their submission in the paper's text. Every submission must include an "AI Use Statement" section, placed before the references (before the reproducibility checklist). This section does not count towards the page limit. A submission without an AI Use Statement will be desk rejected. The AISTATS 2027 paper template includes a boilerplate statement to give authors a sense of the expected level of detail.
L154: Authors are not required to follow this format exactly — these disclosures may be a source of useful information to the community about how AI is affecting research workflows, and we encourage authors to provide as much detail as they want. If no generative AI tools were used, the statement should say so.
L155: Update September 30, 2026: the AI Use Statement only needs to be included in the paper, not in the submission form.
